model: Fan with Yaskawa drive (ProtoNode FPC-N64 profile)
applies_to: Hunter Fans fans whose Yaskawa drive talks Modbus TCP/IP to a Hunter ProtoNode FPC-N64 gateway.
summary: Hunter's ProtoNode FPC-N64 profile for fans with a Yaskawa drive exposes 19 BACnet objects per fan: a command word, speed command and feedback, fault code, motor current, fire relay input and function, communication-loss timeout, reference and run-command source, and the drive's network settings. It is served as BACnet IP or BACnet MS/TP.
notes: XXX in each object name is replaced by the fan's number on the ProtoNode.
The guide prints the Modbus register for each object but no units, ranges or state texts.
No read/write column: access is inferred (AV/BV writable, AI/BI read-only).
By their names, FanXXX/ip1-ip4 and sn1-sn4 carry the drive's IP address and subnet mask octets; the guide does not describe them.

source.title: ProtoNode FPC-N64 Start-up Guide For Interfacing Hunter Fans Products

integration.summary: Write the command and speed command for each fan and read speed feedback, current and the fault code. The communication-loss timeout and reference/run source objects set how the drive reacts to the network.
setup: Each fan drive is its own BACnet device: Device Instance = Node_Offset (default 50,000) + the drive's Node-ID.
The drives talk Modbus TCP/IP to the ProtoNode; enter each drive's ip_address and tcp_id when adding its profile in the web configurator.
Default ProtoNode IP address 192.168.1.24; the ProtoNode serves BACnet IP or BACnet MS/TP to the BMS.
gotchas: The guide does not decode the command word or fault code; use the Yaskawa drive manual.
Network-setting objects (ip, sn, Write) change the drive's own configuration; don't write them from routine BMS logic.
